knowledge:
- key_parameters: taxa_are_rows=Logical indicating whether the OTU table is oriented with taxa as rows (TRUE) or columns (FALSE) ;; measures=Character vector specifying alpha diversity estimators (e.g., "Observed", "Chao1", "ACE", "Shannon", "Simpson", "InvSimpson") ;; method=Character string specifying the ordination method (e.g., "PCoA", "NMDS", "CCA", "DPCoA") ;; distance=Character string or distance object specifying the ecological distance metric (e.g., "bray", "wunifrac", "uunifrac", "jaccard") ;; maxdist=Maximum ecological distance allowed to draw an edge between samples in a network ;; taxlevel=Taxonomic rank at which to merge taxa (e.g., "Genus") ;; speciationMinLength=Threshold patristic distance for merging closely related taxa in tip_glom
- alternatives: picante::unifrac=Alternative package for UniFrac distance, but phyloseq's native UniFrac is optionally-parallelized and faster ;; vegan=Alternative package for ecological distances and ordinations, which phyloseq wraps and extends ;; dada2=Algorithm for sequence-level denoising before importing into phyloseq
- when_to_use: Appropriate when analyzing high-throughput phylogenetic sequencing data clustered into OTUs/ASVs, especially when integrating abundance tables with sample metadata, taxonomic classifications, and phylogenetic trees.
- pitfalls: Rarefying microbiome data is statistically inadmissible and should be avoided; instead, use raw counts for alpha diversity and methods like DESeq2 or relative abundance transformations to handle library size differences ;; Using trimmed/filtered data for richness (alpha diversity) estimates is a mistake; raw, untrimmed OTU data should be used because richness estimates depend heavily on singletons ;; Mixing up the orientation of the OTU table (taxa as rows vs. columns) without setting taxa_are_rows correctly ;; Adding pseudocounts or log-transforming without filtering out highly sparse taxa can lead to unstable downstream ordination or distance calculations.

workflows.name: data_import_and_assembly
workflows.intent: Import raw microbiome data components from various formats and assemble them into a single unified phyloseq object.
workflows.stages: 1. Import BIOM and tree files using import_biom ;; 2. Import sample metadata using import_qiime_sample_data ;; 3. Merge components into a single phyloseq object using merge_phyloseq ;; 4. Alternatively, construct components manually from R matrices/data frames using otu_table, sample_data, tax_table, and read_tree, then combine with phyloseq.
workflows.code:
import_biom(BIOMfilename)
import_qiime_sample_data(map.txt)
merge_phyloseq(x, y)
otu1 <- otu_table(raw_abundance_matrix, taxa_are_rows=FALSE)
sam1 <- sample_data(raw_sample_data.frame)
tax1 <- tax_table(raw_taxonomy_matrix)
tre1 <- read_tree(my_tree_file)
ex1b <- phyloseq(my_otu_table, my_sample_data, my_taxonomyTable, my_tree)
ex1c <- phyloseq(my_otu_table, my_sample_data)

workflows.name: data_filtering_and_transformation
workflows.intent: Filter low-abundance taxa, subset samples or taxonomic groups, transform sample counts, and perform taxonomic or phylogenetic agglomeration.
workflows.stages: 1. Prune taxa based on abundance using prune_taxa and taxa_sums ;; 2. Filter taxa using within-sample criteria with genefilter_sample and filterfun_sample ;; 3. Filter taxa using across-sample criteria with filter_taxa ;; 4. Subset samples based on metadata variables using subset_samples ;; 5. Subset taxa by taxonomic category using subset_taxa ;; 6. Transform abundance counts using transform_sample_counts ;; 7. Agglomerate taxa taxonomically using tax_glom or phylogenetically using tip_glom.
workflows.code:
GP <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(GlobalPatterns) > 0, GlobalPatterns)
most_abundant_taxa <- sort(taxa_sums(GlobalPatterns), TRUE)[1:topN]
ex2 <- prune_taxa(names(most_abundant_taxa), GlobalPatterns)
f1<- filterfun_sample(topp(0.1))
wh1 <- genefilter_sample(GlobalPatterns, f1, A=(1/2*nsamples(GlobalPatterns)))
ex2 <- prune_taxa(wh1, GlobalPatterns)
flist<- filterfun(kOverA(5, 2e-05))
ent.logi <- filter_taxa(enterotype, flist)
ent.trim <- filter_taxa(enterotype, flist, TRUE)
ex3 <- subset_samples(GlobalPatterns, SampleType%in%c("Freshwater", "Ocean", "Freshwater (creek)"))
ex4 <- subset_taxa(GlobalPatterns, Phylum=="Firmicutes")
ex2 <- transform_sample_counts(GlobalPatterns, I)
ex4<- transform_sample_counts(GlobalPatterns, threshrankfun(500))
ex6 <- tax_glom(GlobalPatterns, taxlevel="Genus")
ex7 <- tip_glom(GlobalPatterns, speciationMinLength = 0.05)

workflows.name: exploratory_analysis_and_visualization
workflows.intent: Perform exploratory analysis and generate publication-quality visualizations including alpha diversity plots, phylogenetic trees, bar plots, heatmaps, sample networks, and ordinations.
workflows.stages: 1. Plot alpha diversity estimates using plot_richness ;; 2. Plot annotated phylogenetic trees using plot_tree ;; 3. Generate taxonomic abundance bar plots using plot_bar ;; 4. Create abundance heatmaps using plot_heatmap ;; 5. Construct and plot sample co-occurrence networks using plot_net ;; 6. Calculate ecological distances using distance or UniFrac ;; 7. Perform ordination (PCoA, NMDS, CA, DPCoA) using ordinate and plot results using plot_ordination and plot_scree ;; 8. Perform hierarchical clustering using hclust.
workflows.code:
alpha_meas = c("Observed", "Chao1", "ACE", "Shannon", "Simpson", "InvSimpson")
(p <- plot_richness(GP, "human", "SampleType", measures=alpha_meas))
plot_tree(GP.chl, color="SampleType", shape="Family", label.tips="Genus", size="Abundance")
plot_bar(ent10, "SeqTech", fill="Enterotype", facet_grid=~Genus)
(p <- plot_heatmap(gpac, "NMDS", "bray", "SampleType", "Family"))
plot_net(enterotype, maxdist=0.4, color="SeqTech", shape="Enterotype")
GPUF <- UniFrac(GlobalPatterns)
GloPa.pcoa = ordinate(GlobalPatterns, method="PCoA", distance=GPUF)
plot_scree(GloPa.pcoa, "Scree plot for Global Patterns, UniFrac/PCoA")
(p12 <- plot_ordination(GlobalPatterns, GloPa.pcoa, "samples", color="SampleType") + geom_point(size=5) + geom_path() + scale_colour_hue(guide = FALSE) )
GP.NMDS <- ordinate(GlobalPatterns, "NMDS", GPUF)
gpca <- ordinate(GP, "CCA")
GP.dpcoa <- ordinate(GP, "DPCoA")
pdpcoa <- plot_ordination( physeq = GP, ordination = GP.dpcoa, type="biplot", color="SampleType", shape="Phylum")
distance(esophagus, "bray")
distance(esophagus, "wunifrac")
GP.hclust <- hclust(GPUF, method="average")
plot(GP.hclust, col=cols)

workflows.name: differential_abundance_deseq2
workflows.intent: Convert a phyloseq object to a DESeq2 object to perform negative binomial differential abundance testing and visualize the results.
input: phyloseq_object (An assembled phyloseq S4 object with raw count data)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter out low-read samples and clean up metadata using subset_samples and prune_samples ;; 2. Convert the phyloseq object to a DESeq2 dataset using phyloseq_to_deseq2 ;; 3. Estimate size factors using geometric means and run the DESeq2 pipeline using DESeq ;; 4. Extract and filter significant results using results ;; 5. Merge taxonomic information with test results and plot log2 fold changes.
workflows.code:
kostic <- subset_samples(kostic, DIAGNOSIS != "None")
kostic <- prune_samples(sample_sums(kostic) > 500, kostic)
diagdds = phyloseq_to_deseq2(kostic, ~ DIAGNOSIS)
gm_mean = function(x, na.rm=TRUE){ exp(sum(log(x[x > 0]), na.rm=na.rm) / length(x)) }
geoMeans = apply(counts(diagdds), 1, gm_mean)
diagdds = estimateSizeFactors(diagdds, geoMeans = geoMeans)
diagdds = DESeq(diagdds, fitType="local")
res = results(diagdds)
res = res[order(res$padj, na.last=NA), ]
sigtab = res[(res$padj < alpha), ]
sigtab = cbind(as(sigtab, "data.frame"), as(tax_table(kostic)[rownames(sigtab), ], "matrix"))
ggplot(sigtabgen, aes(y=Genus, x=log2FoldChange, color=Phylum)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0.0, color = "gray", size = 0.5) + geom_point(size=6) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = -90, hjust = 0, vjust=0.5))
